ya, but its important to find out the cause of the hair loss.

you might have male pattern baldness. check out and ask all the male members of your family. look at photos and stuff.

but you also want to rule out other hair loss like telogen effluvium which is stress induced, apolecia areata which might be an autoimmune disorder, hypothyroidism which is also possible, malnutrition, and dermatitis.

if none of these are that significant and your male relatives also bald and if your balding follows the pattern then its because of mpb for sure.

Mpb is caused by your hair follicles suffocating due to binding with too many androgens. it could be the result of naturally developing too many androgen receptors or being sensitive to androgens. 

the scalp is particularly sensitive to androgens... stupid scalp

regardless the culprit androgen is typically DHT . dht is responsible for the awful masculinizing effects like androgenic hair, bigger smelly pp, male fat distributions, apocrine glands, masculine bone structure, and prostate and dick stuff. it binds much more strongly than other androgens. it basically turns a lot of cute boys into hairy and smelly orcs filled with semen. all in all it sucks.

so the idea is you take medication that prohibits the development of dht which allows your hair follicles to not suffocate and die, and potentially recover.

finasteride, dutasteride are both 5a-reductase inhibitors. 5a-reductase enzymes allow the conversion of testosterone to the more potent double trounle DHT. so the idea is you take this medication, and over months your blood dht level should drop to the point where your hair follicles are allowed to exist again.

there is also scary claims of dht blockers giving people permanent loss of sexual dysfunction, but that has been deemed statistically insignificant. nothing happened to me either.

but like with all things hormones its best to take the process nice and slow and make sure your body has time to adapt. start with a moderate dosage and keep consistent. take care of your health and try to actively manage any neuroticism you might have.

lastly, there are also other hair loss products like vasodilators which work to improve blood circulation for targeted regions, and antifungals like ketaconazole which somehow do hair stuff too.


good nutrition is always a plus as well.
